name: Mid
note: INDEX BASE CHANGED. Mid counts the first character as 1; String.Middle counts it as 0. Subtract 1 from the start argument. Mid also clamped a start below 1 to the first character, so Mid(s, 0) was legal and its direct conversion is not; audit loops that start at 0.

name: InStr
note: INDEX BASE AND SENTINEL CHANGED. InStr returns a one-based position and 0 when not found; IndexOf returns a zero-based position and -1 when not found. Rewrite the comparison, do not just rename.

name: InStrB
note: INDEX BASE AND SENTINEL CHANGED, as for InStr.

name: MidB
note: INDEX BASE CHANGED, as for Mid.

name: Redim
note: Not formally deprecated -- the docs (api/language/redim.md) say it exists for Visual Basic compatibility only and to use ResizeTo instead. Array in the replacement stands for the array variable, not a class name: Redim MyPeople(5) becomes MyPeople.ResizeTo(5). Redim is a keyword rather than a class member.

name: Screen Method
note: Screen(i) becomes DesktopDisplay.DisplayAt(i), a shared method with the same zero-based index.

name: Window Method
note: REPLACEMENT CORRECTED BY HAND. The docs page suggests Application.Window, which is itself deprecated on the deprecated Application class. Use DesktopApplication's WindowAt(index) and WindowCount, or iterate App.Windows; WindowAt keeps the zero-based index. The separate Window class row covers the As/New form, which becomes DesktopWindow.

name: Database.Connect
note: Same name; only the error contract changed. The deprecated form returned a Boolean you had to test; the current form returns nothing and raises a DatabaseException on failure. Replace the return-value check with Try/Catch.

name: Date.TotalSeconds
note: EPOCH CHANGED. TotalSeconds counts seconds from 1904-01-01; SecondsFrom1970 counts from 1970-01-01, a difference of 2082844800 seconds. Rebase any stored or transmitted value instead of renaming it. Subtracting two migrated values is safe because the offset cancels. SecondsFrom1970 is read-only; rewrite assignments with the DateTime constructor.

name: FolderItem.AppendToTextFile
note: ERROR MODEL CHANGED, and removed from the framework in 2012r1, so the call is a compile error. AppendToTextFile returned Nil on failure; TextOutputStream.Open(f) raises an IOException instead. Drop the Nil guard, which is now dead code, and wrap the call in Try/Catch. The call moves off the FolderItem, which becomes the argument.
